app.py is a working single-file CLI, 204 lines. Split it into a package, change one internal data structure while you do it, and delete the monolith.

WHAT MUST NOT CHANGE
`python3 -m taskman ...` must reproduce exactly what `python3 app.py ...` prints today, for every subcommand and flag, on stdout, on stderr and in its exit status. app.py's current behaviour IS the specification, including the parts that look like bugs: read select() before you change anything, note when --limit is applied relative to the filters, and keep that. Capture the output of these commands BEFORE you delete app.py and compare afterwards:
  python3 app.py --file data/tasks.tsv list
  python3 app.py --file data/tasks.tsv list --status open --tag work
  python3 app.py --file data/tasks.tsv list --limit 4
  python3 app.py --file data/tasks.tsv list --status open --limit 4
  python3 app.py --file data/tasks.tsv list --sort title --tag urgent
  python3 app.py --file data/tasks.tsv stats
  python3 app.py --file data/tasks.tsv tags
  python3 app.py --file data/tasks.tsv show 12
  python3 app.py --file data/tasks.tsv show 99            (exit 6)
  python3 app.py --file data/tasks.tsv list --status nope  (exit 4)
  python3 app.py --file data/bad.tsv stats                 (exit 5)
  python3 app.py --file data/nope.tsv stats                (exit 3)

TARGET LAYOUT - each name defined in the module named here and nowhere else
- taskman/errors.py: TaskError, BadRow, UnknownStatus unchanged, plus a new UnknownTask(TaskError) constructed as UnknownTask(task_id) and exposing .id
- taskman/models.py: STATUSES and the Task dataclass with its matches() and render() methods
- taskman/store.py: parse_line() and the open_store() context manager
- taskman/index.py: the new TaskIndex class described below
- taskman/report.py: SORT_KEYS and select(), with select()'s signature and behaviour unchanged
- taskman/cli.py: build_parser(), main(argv=None) and the four subcommand functions
- taskman/__main__.py: the `if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main())` entry point and nothing else
- taskman/__init__.py: see LAZY PACKAGE below
- app.py must be DELETED when you are done, and no module may be over 120 lines.

THE REPRESENTATION CHANGE
Today cmd_show finds a task with find(), a linear scan, and cmd_tags and cmd_stats each walk the whole list again. Replace that with an index built once:
  TaskIndex(tasks) - built from an iterable of Task, remembering the order it was given
  .all() -> list of every task in that original order
  .by_id(task_id) -> the Task; raises UnknownTask(task_id) when there is none
  .by_tag(tag) -> list of the tasks carrying that tag, in the original order; an unknown tag gives []
  .tag_counts() -> list of (tag, count, sorted_ids) ordered by count descending then tag ascending, exactly what tag_table() returns today
  .status_counts() -> dict with an entry for EVERY status in STATUSES, zeros included
  .priority_counts() -> dict mapping each priority that occurs to its count
by_id and by_tag must answer without scanning the task list: 60000 tasks and 60000 by_id lookups must take a couple of seconds, not minutes. cmd_show, cmd_tags and cmd_stats must go through a TaskIndex, and the old find() helper must not exist anywhere in the package.

LAZY PACKAGE
`import taskman` must import NO submodule of taskman at all - not errors, not models, not cli. The names Task, STATUSES, TaskError, BadRow, UnknownStatus, UnknownTask, parse_line, open_store, TaskIndex, select and main must still be reachable as attributes of the package, each importing only what it needs at the moment it is first touched. Use a module-level __getattr__ (PEP 562).

IMPORT LAYERING, enforced
  taskman.errors imports nothing from taskman
  taskman.models imports only taskman.errors
  taskman.store imports only taskman.errors and taskman.models
  taskman.index imports only taskman.errors and taskman.models
  taskman.report imports only taskman.errors, taskman.models and taskman.index
  taskman.cli may import any of them

Move the code, do not rewrite it, and do not leave a shim module that re-exports one big file. Standard library only, Python 3.9. Do not modify anything under data/ or tests/. The seeded characterisation suite must pass: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -q

"""Characterisation suite: the behaviour app.py shipped with, pinned.

Do not modify this file. Every expected value here was captured from the monolith
before the split, including the parts that look surprising.
"""
import contextlib
import io
import unittest

import taskman.cli
import taskman.errors
import taskman.index
import taskman.models
import taskman.report
import taskman.store

FILE = ["--file", "data/tasks.tsv"]


def run(argv):
    out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):
        rc = taskman.cli.main(argv)
    return rc, out.getvalue(), err.getvalue()


class TestList(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_default_order_is_priority_then_id(self):
        rc, out, _ = run(FILE + ["list"])
        self.assertEqual(rc, 0)
        self.assertEqual(out, (
            "#2 [done] p1 Ship the report\n"
            "#3 [open] p1 Call the client\n"
            "#8 [open] p1 Buy a filter\n"
            "#11 [done] p1 Pay the deposit\n"
            "#1 [open] p2 Fix the sink\n"
            "#5 [open] p2 Write the spec\n"
            "#7 [done] p2 Send the invoice\n"
            "#9 [blocked] p2 Await legal\n"
            "#12 [open] p2 Draft the r\u00e9sum\u00e9\n"
            "#4 [blocked] p3 Replace the fuse\n"
            "#6 [open] p3 Prune the roses\n"
            "#10 [open] p3 Repot the ficus\n"))

    def test_status_and_tag_filter(self):
        rc, out, _ = run(FILE + ["list", "--status", "open", "--tag", "work"])
        self.assertEqual(out, ("#3 [open] p1 Call the client\n"
                               "#5 [open] p2 Write the spec\n"
                               "#12 [open] p2 Draft the r\u00e9sum\u00e9\n"))

    def test_limit_takes_the_first_rows_of_the_file(self):
        rc, out, _ = run(FILE + ["list", "--limit", "4"])
        self.assertEqual(out, ("#2 [done] p1 Ship the report\n"
                               "#3 [open] p1 Call the client\n"
                               "#1 [open] p2 Fix the sink\n"
                               "#4 [blocked] p3 Replace the fuse\n"))

    def test_limit_is_applied_before_the_filters(self):
        # Four rows are read, then the status filter removes two of them, so this
        # prints two lines and not four. That is what the monolith does.
        rc, out, _ = run(FILE + ["list", "--status", "open", "--limit", "4"])
        self.assertEqual(out, ("#3 [open] p1 Call the client\n"
                               "#1 [open] p2 Fix the sink\n"))

    def test_sort_title_then_id(self):
        rc, out, _ = run(FILE + ["list", "--sort", "title", "--tag", "urgent"])
        self.assertEqual(out, ("#3 [open] p1 Call the client\n"
                               "#1 [open] p2 Fix the sink\n"
                               "#11 [done] p1 Pay the deposit\n"
                               "#7 [done] p2 Send the invoice\n"))

    def test_sort_id(self):
        rc, out, _ = run(FILE + ["list", "--tag", "garden", "--sort", "id"])
        self.assertEqual(out, ("#6 [open] p3 Prune the roses\n"
                               "#10 [open] p3 Repot the ficus\n"))

    def test_limit_zero_prints_nothing(self):
        rc, out, _ = run(FILE + ["list", "--limit", "0"])
        self.assertEqual((rc, out), (0, ""))

    def test_unknown_status_exits_four(self):
        rc, out, err = run(FILE + ["list", "--status", "nope"])
        self.assertEqual(rc, 4)
        self.assertEqual(out, "")
        self.assertEqual(err, "error: unknown status 'nope'\n")


class TestOtherCommands(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_stats(self):
        rc, out, _ = run(FILE + ["stats"])
        self.assertEqual(out, "open=7 done=3 blocked=2\ntotal=12\np1=4 p2=5 p3=3\n")

    def test_tags(self):
        rc, out, _ = run(FILE + ["tags"])
        self.assertEqual(out, ("work 6 2,3,5,7,9,12\n"
                               "home 5 1,4,8,10,12\n"
                               "urgent 4 1,3,7,11\n"
                               "garden 2 6,10\n"))

    def test_show(self):
        rc, out, _ = run(FILE + ["show", "12"])
        self.assertEqual(out, ("id: 12\nstatus: open\npriority: 2\n"
                               "tags: work, home\ntitle: Draft the r\u00e9sum\u00e9\n"))

    def test_show_missing_id_exits_six(self):
        rc, out, err = run(FILE + ["show", "99"])
        self.assertEqual((rc, out, err), (6, "", "error: no task 99\n"))

    def test_bad_row_exits_five(self):
        rc, out, err = run(["--file", "data/bad.tsv", "stats"])
        self.assertEqual((rc, out, err), (5, "", "error: bad row on line 3\n"))

    def test_missing_file_exits_three(self):
        rc, out, err = run(["--file", "data/nope.tsv", "stats"])
        self.assertEqual((rc, out, err), (3, "", "error: cannot read data/nope.tsv\n"))


class TestPiecesStayedWhereTheyWere(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_parse_line_rejects_a_short_row(self):
        with self.assertRaises(taskman.errors.BadRow) as ctx:
            taskman.store.parse_line("1\topen\t1\n", 7)
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.line, 7)

    def test_parse_line_rejects_an_unknown_status(self):
        with self.assertRaises(taskman.errors.BadRow):
            taskman.store.parse_line("1\tsomehow\t1\thome\tTitle\n", 2)

    def test_parse_line_rejects_a_blank_title(self):
        with self.assertRaises(taskman.errors.BadRow):
            taskman.store.parse_line("1\topen\t1\thome\t   \n", 2)

    def test_parse_line_drops_empty_tags(self):
        t = taskman.store.parse_line("4\topen\t2\t a , ,b \tThing\n", 2)
        self.assertEqual(t.tags, ["a", "b"])

    def test_task_matches(self):
        t = taskman.models.Task(9, "open", 1, ["home"], "probe")
        self.assertTrue(t.matches(status="open"))
        self.assertFalse(t.matches(status="done"))
        self.assertTrue(t.matches(tag="home"))
        self.assertFalse(t.matches(tag="work"))
        self.assertTrue(t.matches())

    def test_open_store_yields_every_row(self):
        with taskman.store.open_store("data/tasks.tsv") as tasks:
            self.assertEqual([t.id for t in tasks], list(range(1, 13)))

    def test_select_keeps_its_signature(self):
        with taskman.store.open_store("data/tasks.tsv") as tasks:
            rows = taskman.report.select(tasks, status="open", limit=4)
        self.assertEqual([t.id for t in rows], [3, 1])


class TestIndex(unittest.TestCase):
    def build(self):
        with taskman.store.open_store("data/tasks.tsv") as tasks:
            return taskman.index.TaskIndex(tasks)

    def test_all_keeps_file_order(self):
        self.assertEqual([t.id for t in self.build().all()], list(range(1, 13)))

    def test_by_id(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.build().by_id(7).title, "Send the invoice")

    def test_by_id_unknown_raises(self):
        with self.assertRaises(taskman.errors.UnknownTask) as ctx:
            self.build().by_id(99)
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.id, 99)
        self.assertTrue(issubclass(taskman.errors.UnknownTask, taskman.errors.TaskError))

    def test_by_tag_keeps_file_order(self):
        self.assertEqual([t.id for t in self.build().by_tag("home")], [1, 4, 8, 10, 12])

    def test_by_tag_unknown_is_empty(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.build().by_tag("nothing"), [])

    def test_tag_counts(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.build().tag_counts(), [
            ("work", 6, [2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 12]),
            ("home", 5, [1, 4, 8, 10, 12]),
            ("urgent", 4, [1, 3, 7, 11]),
            ("garden", 2, [6, 10]),
        ])

    def test_status_counts_includes_zeroes(self):
        idx = taskman.index.TaskIndex([taskman.models.Task(1, "open", 1, [], "x")])
        self.assertEqual(idx.status_counts(), {"open": 1, "done": 0, "blocked": 0})

    def test_priority_counts(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.build().priority_counts(), {1: 4, 2: 5, 3: 3})

    def test_empty_index(self):
        idx = taskman.index.TaskIndex([])
        self.assertEqual(idx.all(), [])
        self.assertEqual(idx.tag_counts(), [])
        self.assertEqual(idx.priority_counts(), {})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
